identity.variant: standard triangular patch with three color boundaries

card.description: A self-dual CSS family cut from the hexagonal tiling: data qubits occupy vertices, and every three-colored face carries both an X check and a Z check on the same support. The finite patch has one red, one green, and one blue boundary, so same-colored strings may terminate while a boundary-to-boundary string remains logical. The constructor fixes the standard odd-distance triangle explicitly; the bulk label 6.6.6 alone would not specify those finite boundaries or the qubit count.

views.description: Expanding the selected triangular face boundaries gives identical binary X- and Z-check matrices. Their sparse symplectic rows are the universal executable object used for commutation, rank, logical, and small-distance checks.

Remove every third point from an integer triangular index grid and read the removed points as face centers. The six surrounding sites form a bulk hexagon, while clipping at the three sides gives boundary faces. The resulting face-incidence matrix is used for both X and Z checks; even face weights and even pairwise overlaps make the CSS commutation visible before any rank calculation.

Red, green, and blue strings are deformable by multiplying face checks. A colored string may end only on the matching color boundary. In the triangular patch, representatives of different colors and Pauli types describe one protected logical pair rather than three independent qubits.

A local Clifford unfolding turns the triangular color-code data into attached surface-code sheets. The three color boundaries become a folded arrangement of rough and smooth boundary sectors, explaining why color-code strings branch while the unfolded strings look surface-code-like.

With perfect syndrome, maximum-likelihood decoding maps to a random three-body Ising problem: one data-qubit error couples the three colored checks meeting that vertex. The dictionary exposes correlations that a naive independent matching of defect pairs would discard.

A boundary is specified by which anyons condense there, not merely by the pigment used in a drawing. This separates the three color boundaries used by this constructor from Pauli boundaries and gives a precise language for surgery interfaces and domain walls.

The two-dimensional locality-preserving gate bound stops at the Clifford level. The color code saturates that useful level through its transversal Clifford structure, but universality needs a mechanism such as injection, distillation, switching, or surgery that is not one constant-depth local gate on the isolated patch.

Small color-code encoding tensors can be contracted and their logical operators pushed through the network. Contraction constructs a new larger code with its own boundary data; it is not permission to infer a finite 6.6.6 patch from the bulk tiling name alone.

params.distance: Odd code distance at least three; also the weight of the constructor's left-boundary logical X and Z representatives.
params.boundary: Exact finite-patch convention. The supported literal is 'three-color-triangle'; other 6.6.6 boundaries define different families.

decoders.noise: code-capacity Pauli noise with perfect syndrome on a three-color triangular boundary
decoders.notes: Projection or restriction turns each color-pair sector into a surface-code matching problem, then a lifting step reconciles the correlated projections into one color-code correction. Boundary connected components are part of the algorithm; applying the closed-surface lifting rule unchanged can reduce the effective distance.

decoders.notes: Möbius matching folds the three boundary sectors into a single graph so that a pairing can cross the seam instead of choosing three independent color projections. Its numerical performance is decoder- and noise-model-specific, so this entry does not attach a bare threshold to the check matrix.

decoders.noise: repeated circuit-level syndrome extraction with detector events, correlated faults, and a specified measurement schedule

realizations.description: The smallest triangular member was encoded and used for logical operations. This realizes the Steane/color-code intersection at fixed distance, not growth of the 6.6.6 family.

Fault-tolerant Clifford primitives on small color-code blocks were combined with logical magic-state preparation and injection. The universal protocol includes the injected resource; it is not a universal transversal gate set of one two-dimensional patch.

Many small color-code blocks were moved and coupled through transversal logical operations inside a larger architecture. The experiment is a multi-block operation result, not an increasing-distance memory test.

Two finite code sizes were operated with repeated syndrome extraction, hardware-specific decoding, transversal Clifford gates, magic-state injection, and logical teleportation by surgery. Size scaling, gate benchmarks, and surgery are distinct claims with distinct observables.

Local Clifford unfolding maps a closed 2D color code to two surface-code copies; for the triangular boundary, the copies remain attached along a fold. This is an equivalence dictionary, not the constructor recipe used for the exact face-incidence matrix here.

The 6.6.6 and 4.8.8 tilings realize the same abstract 2D color-code order, while face weights, finite-boundary staircases, qubit counts, and extraction circuits differ and must not be transferred numerically.

# 6.6.6 color code (three-color triangular boundary)

## Essence

**The object.** Start from a honeycomb tiling, put data qubits on its
vertices, and color the faces red, green, and blue so that neighboring faces
have different colors. Every retained face `f` carries two checks on the same
vertex set,

`X_f = product of X on the vertices of f`,

`Z_f = product of Z on the vertices of f`.

The entry fixes one finite family rather than the bulk tiling alone: an
odd-distance triangular patch with one boundary of each color. Bulk faces
have six vertices and clipped boundary faces have four. The binary face
incidence matrix `H` is used twice, `H_X=H_Z=H`, so the code is a self-dual
CSS code. The [face-incidence derivation](pedagogy/face-incidence-and-parameters.md)
turns the constructor's integer-grid rule into the exact family ledger

`n=(3d^2+1)/4`, `number of faces=3(d^2-1)/8`, and `k=1`.

For the shipped patches the Atlas verifies `[[7,1,3]]` and `[[19,1,5]]`
exactly. It recomputes `n=37` and `k=1` for the distance-seven patch, while
its distance remains literature-claimed because the shared verifier does not
yet carry a general lower-bound certificate at that size. The distinction is
recorded on the [logical and distance page](pedagogy/boundaries-logicals-and-distance.md)
and routed to the [distance-certificate gap](../../wanted.html#certified-lower-bounds).

**The trick.** A face color and a Pauli type are independent labels. A green
hexagon supports both one X check and one Z check. The three face colors tell
you how string excitations branch, deform, and terminate at boundaries;
X versus Z tells you which Pauli sector is being checked. Keeping those axes
separate is the shortest route through most color-code notation.

**One sentence.** The triangular 6.6.6 color code uses one three-colored
vertex-face incidence pattern for both CSS sectors, leaving one conjugate
pair of boundary logical strings and a transversal Clifford structure.

## Design problem

A two-dimensional topological memory wants local bounded-weight checks while
its logical operators grow with the patch. A surface-code face has one Pauli
role: primal and dual cellulations carry different check sectors. The color
code asks whether one cellulation can support both sectors and thereby make
some logical symmetries literal physical symmetries.

Three geometric conditions make that possible:

1. data qubits sit on vertices of a trivalent graph;
2. faces admit three colors, with unlike colors across every shared edge;
3. every retained face has even weight, and two distinct faces meet on zero
   or two vertices.

The last condition gives `H H^T=0` over `F_2`. Thus the same matrix may be
used for X and Z checks without violating commutation. Because the two check
families have identical support, physical Hadamard exchanges them. Because
the vertex graph is bipartite, alternating `S` and `S-dagger` preserves every
face pair and implements a phase gate in the declared logical convention.
Pairwise CNOT between aligned blocks follows from the ordinary CSS
conjugation rules. The
[Clifford operations page](pedagogy/transversal-clifford-and-operations.md)
derives those ideal Pauli maps and keeps routing, syndrome extraction, and
recovery outside the word "transversal."

The design buys more symmetry, not a free universal gate set. A
bounded-depth, bounded-range logical gate on a growing-distance 2D local
stabilizer family is Clifford by the
[Bravyi–König theorem](../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-koenig.md). A logical
non-Clifford operation therefore needs injection, distillation, switching,
surgery, or another mechanism that supplies an extra resource or leaves the
theorem's assumptions.

The finite boundary is also part of the code, not packaging. The label
`6.6.6` specifies that three hexagons meet at a bulk vertex. It does not
specify which faces are clipped, which excitations condense, how many logical
qubits remain, or the qubit-count formula. This entry's literal boundary
parameter is `three-color-triangle`; a torus, a Pauli-boundary patch, and a
different triangular staircase are different formal objects.

## Derivation chain

**1. Build a triangular index set.** Write `d=2t+1` and take integer points
`(r,c)` satisfying `0<=c<=r<=3t`. In row `r`, mark a face center when
`c mod 3 = 2-(r mod 3)` and treat every other point as a data vertex. The six
fixed offsets around a face center list its bulk vertices; clipping those
offsets against the triangle produces weight-four boundary faces.

**2. Count faces and qubits.** Rows `3a`, `3a+1`, and `3a+2` contain
respectively `a`, `a+1`, and `a+1` face centers. Summing the complete row
triples gives `3t(t+1)/2` faces. Subtracting them from all integer points in
the triangle leaves `3t^2+3t+1` data vertices. Replacing `t=(d-1)/2` gives
the formulas in Essence.

**3. Use one incidence matrix twice.** Let `H[f,q]=1` exactly when data qubit
`q` lies on face `f`. Every row has weight four or six. Distinct rows overlap
on either no vertex or the two endpoints of one shared edge. Therefore every
entry of `H H^T` is even, so `H_X H_Z^T=0` when `H_X=H_Z=H`.

**4. Count the logical dimension.** Boundary peeling makes the face rows
independent: any nonempty mod-two sum has an outermost retained face whose
exposed boundary vertex is not canceled; remove that layer and repeat. If
`m=3(d^2-1)/8`, the X and Z halves therefore contribute `2m` independent
stabilizers. Since `n-2m=1`, the patch encodes one qubit. The reproduction
transcript independently runs GF(2) elimination on all three shipped
instances.

**5. Exhibit the logical pair.** Put X on the `d` data vertices of the left
side. Every face meets that side evenly, so the operator commutes with all Z
checks. It is not an X stabilizer because the same support filled with Z
overlaps it on odd `d` sites. The X and Z boundary strings therefore
anticommute and form one logical pair. This proves an upper bound `d_code<=d`.

**6. Separate the upper witness from the lower bound.** A drawn weight-`d`
string never proves that no lighter logical exists. Exact CSS enumeration
closes both sides for `d=3` and `d=5`. For `d=7`, the Atlas recomputes the
weight-seven witness but retains the cited family lower bound as a
`claimed` origin. The
[distance ledger](pedagogy/boundaries-logicals-and-distance.md) shows exactly
where computation stops and literature begins.

**7. Decode the correlations you actually measured.** One data-qubit Pauli
fault touches the three colored faces meeting that vertex in the bulk. A
projection decoder turns color-pair sectors into surface-code matching
problems and then lifts a compatible correction. A Möbius decoder instead
folds all three triangular boundary sectors into one nonorientable matching
graph. With repeated extraction, detector events and correlated circuit
faults replace the static syndrome. The
[decoding page](pedagogy/decoding-and-syndrome-extraction.md) keeps these
inputs separate.

**8. Read operations from the same algebra.** Physical H swaps every paired
`X_f,Z_f`. Alternating `S` on even row-major qubits with `S-dagger` on odd
ones sends `X_f` to `X_f Z_f` with no residual face phase and sends the
declared logical X to `i X_L Z_L`. Pairwise physical CNOT gives the CSS
logical CNOT map. Surgery and magic-state protocols are then additional
spacetime constructions, not more consequences of `H_X=H_Z`.

## Multiple pictures

- **Sparse CSS matrix.** `H_X=H_Z=H` is the universal executable picture.
  It decides commutation, rank, the finite logical quotient, exact small
  distances, and the incidence scene without relying on a drawing.

- **Three-colored strings.** Multiplying a face check deforms a string without
  changing its logical action. Color labels track which endpoint excitation
  can terminate at which boundary. The three color sectors describe one
  protected Pauli pair on this triangle, not three encoded qubits.

- **Anyon condensation.** A boundary is specified by the excitations it can
  absorb. This language distinguishes a color boundary from a Pauli boundary
  even when both are drawn as an edge, and it makes surgery interfaces a
  statement about condensed sectors rather than pigments.

- **Folded surface codes.** A local Clifford unfolding maps color-code data to
  surface-code sheets. For a triangular boundary the sheets remain attached
  along a fold. The dictionary explains why colored strings may branch while
  projected decoder strings look pairwise, but it does not make this
  constructor an exact surface-code construction replay.

- **Random three-body Ising model.** Under perfect syndrome, a data-qubit
  error couples the three colored checks meeting that vertex. Maximum-
  likelihood decoding becomes an order-disorder problem with three-body
  interactions, exposing the correlations that independent pair matchings
  would discard.

- **Circuit and detector graph.** In repeated extraction the objects being
  matched are changes between measured check outcomes, not static face
  defects. Flag, superdense, and middle-out circuits create different fault
  correlations and therefore different detector graphs.

- **Tensor network.** A small color-code encoder can be viewed as a tensor;
  operator pushing recovers its stabilizer and logical action. Contracting
  tensors creates a new code whose boundary and parameters must be computed,
  not inherited from the original block.

The [representation and realization ledger](pedagogy/representations-variants-and-realizations.md)
states what each dictionary preserves. The guided
[face-to-boundary tour](../../tours/color_666.html) lets the reader switch the
constructor-derived distance-three and distance-five scenes among face color,
Pauli incidence, and logical-string modes.

## Why these parameters

**Why odd `d`.** The chosen triangular staircase has side support of odd
length. That makes the X and Z representatives on the same side overlap
oddly and therefore anticommute. The constructor rejects even inputs rather
than silently switching to another boundary family.

**Why `n=(3d^2+1)/4`.** For `d=2t+1`, the integer triangle contains
`(3t+1)(3t+2)/2` positions and the modular rule marks `3t(t+1)/2` of them as
face centers. The remainder is `3t^2+3t+1` data qubits. This is a
boundary-specific count, not a consequence of the bulk Schläfli symbol by
itself.

**Why `k=1`.** There are `m=3(d^2-1)/8` independent face supports. Each
appears once in the X sector and once in the Z sector, so the stabilizer rank
is `2m`. Substitution gives `k=n-2m=1`. The red, green, and blue string
descriptions are related representatives of that one quotient.

**Why the declared logical has weight `d`.** The left side contains one data
site at each step of the boundary staircase after face centers are removed.
Every adjacent face meets it on zero or two sites. The support therefore has
zero syndrome, and its X/Z copies anticommute because `d` is odd.

**Why the code distance is not automatically verified at every `d`.** The
boundary string supplies only an upper witness. A lower bound must exclude
every lighter normalizer element outside the stabilizer row space. The shared
exact enumerator does that for the seven- and nineteen-qubit instances, but
the thirty-seven-qubit member uses the fetch-verified triangular-family
result of Chamberland et al. rather than pretending an unavailable machine
certificate exists.

**Why the family is qLDPC but low-rate.** Face-check weight is at most six and
each bulk qubit touches three faces in each Pauli sector, independent of `d`.
The family therefore has bounded local degrees, while `k=1` and
`n=Theta(d^2)` make its rate vanish. Bounded check weight does not imply
positive rate.

## Failure modes

- **Equating face color with Pauli type.** A red face is not an X check. The
  red face supports both an X check and a Z check. Color labels topological
  string sectors; Pauli labels CSS sectors.

- **Reading `6.6.6` as a finite specification.** The bulk symbol does not
  determine boundary clipping, `n`, `k`, or the logical basis. Numerical
  claims from another triangular staircase, a torus, or a 4.8.8 patch do not
  transfer automatically.

- **Counting three colors as three logical qubits.** Face checks deform
  colored string representatives into one another. Direct rank gives one
  protected qubit for this boundary, and the declared X/Z pair already spans
  its logical Pauli algebra.

- **Calling a weight-`d` string a distance proof.** It proves `d_code<=d`.
  The reverse inequality is an exact enumeration or a cited family theorem,
  and its provenance must remain visible.

- **Matching color sectors independently and stopping.** Projection creates
  correlated surface-code problems. A lifting or reconciliation step is
  required, and triangular boundary components must be handled explicitly.

- **Moving a code-capacity threshold into a circuit claim.** Perfect-syndrome
  Pauli noise, faulty measurements, a scheduled extraction circuit, and a
  hardware experiment have different elementary events and decoder inputs.
  As of the 2026-08-02 decoder sweep, the entry has no threshold identity
  tuple safe enough to attach as a bare family number.

- **Calling transversal Clifford gates universal.** H, phase, and inter-block
  CNOT generate the Clifford group. Universality in the cited experiments
  includes injected or prepared magic states and feed-forward.

- **Treating unfolding as an exact constructor recipe.** The literature gives
  a local-Clifford equivalence dictionary. The repository has no registered
  exact operation-tree adapter for this finite face-incidence convention, so
  the card honestly omits `construction:`.

## Operations story

**Hadamard.** Physical H on every data qubit maps `X_f` to `Z_f` and `Z_f`
to `X_f`. Since the two face-support matrices are identical, the stabilizer
group is preserved. The same conjugation swaps the declared left-boundary
logical X and Z, so it is logical H in this basis.

**Phase.** The physical vertex graph is bipartite. In the constructor's
row-major order the two parts are the even- and odd-numbered qubits. Apply S
on the even part and `S-dagger` on the odd part. Every retained face has equal
numbers from the two parts, so the conjugated X check is exactly `X_f Z_f`
with its phase canceled. The odd left boundary contains one more even site,
so `X_L` maps to `i X_L Z_L` while `Z_L` stays fixed: logical S in the
declared convention. Reversing the bipartition implements the dagger.

**Pairwise CNOT.** Align two identical patches and apply a physical CNOT to
each corresponding pair. Control X checks acquire the matching target X
check, target Z checks acquire the matching control Z check, and the other
two check types remain fixed. The boundary logical pair undergoes the same
CNOT conjugation. Physical alignment, transport, extraction, and recovery
remain additional costs.

**Lattice surgery.** Compatible colored or Pauli boundary sectors can be
joined by a temporary strip of checks whose product measures a joint logical
Pauli. Fault tolerance requires repeated seam extraction, spacetime decoding,
and a Pauli-frame update. The low-overhead cited layout deliberately mixes
6.6.6 and 4.8.8 regions, so its resource result is not a property of an
isolated 6.6.6 memory.

**Non-Clifford completion.** A prepared or distilled magic state, logical
Pauli measurement, and feed-forward supply the non-Clifford resource. The
fixed-block trapped-ion and multi-distance superconducting demonstrations
combine these resources with color-code Clifford operations; they do not
demonstrate a universal transversal gate set on one 2D patch. The
[operations ledger](pedagogy/transversal-clifford-and-operations.md) separates
the ideal code automorphisms from these protocol and hardware layers.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why may the same face support define both an X check and a Z check?
**A:** Every face has even weight and distinct faces overlap on zero or two
vertices, so `H H^T=0` over `F_2`. The X/Z symplectic overlap is therefore
even for every pair.

**Q2:** Why does a red face not mean an X-type stabilizer? **A:** Red is one
of three geometric face colors and controls the colored-string dictionary.
That red support appears once as an X stabilizer and again as a Z stabilizer;
Pauli type is a separate label.

**Q3:** How do the formulas `n=(3d^2+1)/4` and `k=1` know about the boundary?
**A:** They count the retained vertices and independent clipped faces of this
specific modular triangular staircase. A different cut changes those counts
even if its bulk faces are also hexagons.

**Q4:** What does the left-boundary string prove about distance? **A:** Its
weight `d`, zero syndrome, and anticommutation with the conjugate string prove
an upper bound. Exact enumeration supplies the lower bound for `d=3,5`; the
distance-seven lower bound remains cited and claimed.

**Q5:** Why is a surface-code projection not already a color-code decoder?
**A:** One physical error contributes to several color-pair projections. The
projected matches are correlated and must be lifted to one correction whose
full color-code syndrome is correct, including the triangular boundaries.

**Q6:** Why does alternating S and `S-dagger` preserve an X face check?
**A:** Each four- or six-vertex face contains equal numbers from the two
bipartition classes. The local conjugation phases cancel and the result is
`X_f Z_f`, the product of two existing stabilizers on that face.

**Q7:** Do transversal H, S, and CNOT make the family universal? **A:** No.
They generate Clifford operations. A non-Clifford gate in the cited protocols
comes from a magic state, injection, distillation, switching, surgery, or
another resource outside the isolated constant-depth 2D stabilizer gate.

**Q8:** What exactly was demonstrated at distance three? **A:** The
seven-qubit patch is also the Steane block, so fixed-block experiments verify
encoded operations on the smallest family member. They do not by themselves
demonstrate increasing-distance suppression across the 6.6.6 family.

qubits remain, or the qubit-count formula. This entry's literal boundary
parameter is `three-color-triangle`; a torus, a Pauli-boundary patch, and a
different triangular staircase are different formal objects.

## Derivation chain

**1. Build a triangular index set.** Write `d=2t+1` and take integer points
`(r,c)` satisfying `0<=c<=r<=3t`. In row `r`, mark a face center when
`c mod 3 = 2-(r mod 3)` and treat every other point as a data vertex. The six
fixed offsets around a face center list its bulk vertices; clipping those
offsets against the triangle produces weight-four boundary faces.

**2. Count faces and qubits.** Rows `3a`, `3a+1`, and `3a+2` contain
respectively `a`, `a+1`, and `a+1` face centers. Summing the complete row
triples gives `3t(t+1)/2` faces. Subtracting them from all integer points in
the triangle leaves `3t^2+3t+1` data vertices. Replacing `t=(d-1)/2` gives
the formulas in Essence.

**3. Use one incidence matrix twice.** Let `H[f,q]=1` exactly when data qubit
`q` lies on face `f`. Every row has weight four or six. Distinct rows overlap
on either no vertex or the two endpoints of one shared edge. Therefore every
entry of `H H^T` is even, so `H_X H_Z^T=0` when `H_X=H_Z=H`.

**4. Count the logical dimension.** Boundary peeling makes the face rows
independent: any nonempty mod-two sum has an outermost retained face whose
exposed boundary vertex is not canceled; remove that layer and repeat. If
`m=3(d^2-1)/8`, the X and Z halves therefore contribute `2m` independent
stabilizers. Since `n-2m=1`, the patch encodes one qubit. The reproduction
transcript independently runs GF(2) elimination on all three shipped
instances.

**5. Exhibit the logical pair.** Put X on the `d` data vertices of the left
side. Every face meets that side evenly, so the operator commutes with all Z
checks. It is not an X stabilizer because the same support filled with Z
overlaps it on odd `d` sites. The X and Z boundary strings therefore
anticommute and form one logical pair. This proves an upper bound `d_code<=d`.

**6. Separate the upper witness from the lower bound.** A drawn weight-`d`
string never proves that no lighter logical exists. Exact CSS enumeration
closes both sides for `d=3` and `d=5`. For `d=7`, the Atlas recomputes the
weight-seven witness but retains the cited family lower bound as a
`claimed` origin. The
[distance ledger](pedagogy/boundaries-logicals-and-distance.md) shows exactly
where computation stops and literature begins.

**7. Decode the correlations you actually measured.** One data-qubit Pauli
fault touches the three colored faces meeting that vertex in the bulk. A
projection decoder turns color-pair sectors into surface-code matching
problems and then lifts a compatible correction. A Möbius decoder instead
folds all three triangular boundary sectors into one nonorientable matching
graph. With repeated extraction, detector events and correlated circuit
faults replace the static syndrome. The
[decoding page](pedagogy/decoding-and-syndrome-extraction.md) keeps these
inputs separate.

**8. Read operations from the same algebra.** Physical H swaps every paired
`X_f,Z_f`. Alternating `S` on even row-major qubits with `S-dagger` on odd
ones sends `X_f` to `X_f Z_f` with no residual face phase and sends the
declared logical X to `i X_L Z_L`. Pairwise physical CNOT gives the CSS
logical CNOT map. Surgery and magic-state protocols are then additional
spacetime constructions, not more consequences of `H_X=H_Z`.

## Multiple pictures

- **Sparse CSS matrix.** `H_X=H_Z=H` is the universal executable picture.
  It decides commutation, rank, the finite logical quotient, exact small
  distances, and the incidence scene without relying on a drawing.

- **Three-colored strings.** Multiplying a face check deforms a string without
  changing its logical action. Color labels track which endpoint excitation
  can terminate at which boundary. The three color sectors describe one
  protected Pauli pair on this triangle, not three encoded qubits.

- **Anyon condensation.** A boundary is specified by the excitations it can
  absorb. This language distinguishes a color boundary from a Pauli boundary
  even when both are drawn as an edge, and it makes surgery interfaces a
  statement about condensed sectors rather than pigments.

- **Folded surface codes.** A local Clifford unfolding maps color-code data to
  surface-code sheets. For a triangular boundary the sheets remain attached
  along a fold. The dictionary explains why colored strings may branch while
  projected decoder strings look pairwise, but it does not make this
  constructor an exact surface-code construction replay.

- **Random three-body Ising model.** Under perfect syndrome, a data-qubit
  error couples the three colored checks meeting that vertex. Maximum-
  likelihood decoding becomes an order-disorder problem with three-body
  interactions, exposing the correlations that independent pair matchings
  would discard.

- **Circuit and detector graph.** In repeated extraction the objects being
  matched are changes between measured check outcomes, not static face
  defects. Flag, superdense, and middle-out circuits create different fault
  correlations and therefore different detector graphs.

- **Tensor network.** A small color-code encoder can be viewed as a tensor;
  operator pushing recovers its stabilizer and logical action. Contracting
  tensors creates a new code whose boundary and parameters must be computed,
  not inherited from the original block.

The [representation and realization ledger](pedagogy/representations-variants-and-realizations.md)
states what each dictionary preserves. The guided
[face-to-boundary tour](../../tours/color_666.html) lets the reader switch the
constructor-derived distance-three and distance-five scenes among face color,
Pauli incidence, and logical-string modes.

## Why these parameters

**Why odd `d`.** The chosen triangular staircase has side support of odd
length. That makes the X and Z representatives on the same side overlap
oddly and therefore anticommute. The constructor rejects even inputs rather
than silently switching to another boundary family.

**Why `n=(3d^2+1)/4`.** For `d=2t+1`, the integer triangle contains
`(3t+1)(3t+2)/2` positions and the modular rule marks `3t(t+1)/2` of them as
face centers. The remainder is `3t^2+3t+1` data qubits. This is a
boundary-specific count, not a consequence of the bulk Schläfli symbol by
itself.

**Why `k=1`.** There are `m=3(d^2-1)/8` independent face supports. Each
appears once in the X sector and once in the Z sector, so the stabilizer rank
is `2m`. Substitution gives `k=n-2m=1`. The red, green, and blue string
descriptions are related representatives of that one quotient.

**Why the declared logical has weight `d`.** The left side contains one data
site at each step of the boundary staircase after face centers are removed.
Every adjacent face meets it on zero or two sites. The support therefore has
zero syndrome, and its X/Z copies anticommute because `d` is odd.

**Why the code distance is not automatically verified at every `d`.** The
boundary string supplies only an upper witness. A lower bound must exclude
every lighter normalizer element outside the stabilizer row space. The shared
exact enumerator does that for the seven- and nineteen-qubit instances, but
the thirty-seven-qubit member uses the fetch-verified triangular-family
result of Chamberland et al. rather than pretending an unavailable machine
certificate exists.

**Why the family is qLDPC but low-rate.** Face-check weight is at most six and
each bulk qubit touches three faces in each Pauli sector, independent of `d`.
The family therefore has bounded local degrees, while `k=1` and
`n=Theta(d^2)` make its rate vanish. Bounded check weight does not imply
positive rate.

## Failure modes

- **Equating face color with Pauli type.** A red face is not an X check. The
  red face supports both an X check and a Z check. Color labels topological
  string sectors; Pauli labels CSS sectors.

- **Reading `6.6.6` as a finite specification.** The bulk symbol does not
  determine boundary clipping, `n`, `k`, or the logical basis. Numerical
  claims from another triangular staircase, a torus, or a 4.8.8 patch do not
  transfer automatically.

- **Counting three colors as three logical qubits.** Face checks deform
  colored string representatives into one another. Direct rank gives one
  protected qubit for this boundary, and the declared X/Z pair already spans
  its logical Pauli algebra.

- **Calling a weight-`d` string a distance proof.** It proves `d_code<=d`.
  The reverse inequality is an exact enumeration or a cited family theorem,
  and its provenance must remain visible.

- **Matching color sectors independently and stopping.** Projection creates
  correlated surface-code problems. A lifting or reconciliation step is
  required, and triangular boundary components must be handled explicitly.

- **Moving a code-capacity threshold into a circuit claim.** Perfect-syndrome
  Pauli noise, faulty measurements, a scheduled extraction circuit, and a
  hardware experiment have different elementary events and decoder inputs.
  As of the 2026-08-02 decoder sweep, the entry has no threshold identity
  tuple safe enough to attach as a bare family number.

- **Calling transversal Clifford gates universal.** H, phase, and inter-block
  CNOT generate the Clifford group. Universality in the cited experiments
  includes injected or prepared magic states and feed-forward.

- **Treating unfolding as an exact constructor recipe.** The literature gives
  a local-Clifford equivalence dictionary. The repository has no registered
  exact operation-tree adapter for this finite face-incidence convention, so
  the card honestly omits `construction:`.

## Operations story

**Hadamard.** Physical H on every data qubit maps `X_f` to `Z_f` and `Z_f`
to `X_f`. Since the two face-support matrices are identical, the stabilizer
group is preserved. The same conjugation swaps the declared left-boundary
logical X and Z, so it is logical H in this basis.

**Phase.** The physical vertex graph is bipartite. In the constructor's
row-major order the two parts are the even- and odd-numbered qubits. Apply S
on the even part and `S-dagger` on the odd part. Every retained face has equal
numbers from the two parts, so the conjugated X check is exactly `X_f Z_f`
with its phase canceled. The odd left boundary contains one more even site,
so `X_L` maps to `i X_L Z_L` while `Z_L` stays fixed: logical S in the
declared convention. Reversing the bipartition implements the dagger.

**Pairwise CNOT.** Align two identical patches and apply a physical CNOT to
each corresponding pair. Control X checks acquire the matching target X
check, target Z checks acquire the matching control Z check, and the other
two check types remain fixed. The boundary logical pair undergoes the same
CNOT conjugation. Physical alignment, transport, extraction, and recovery
remain additional costs.

**Lattice surgery.** Compatible colored or Pauli boundary sectors can be
joined by a temporary strip of checks whose product measures a joint logical
Pauli. Fault tolerance requires repeated seam extraction, spacetime decoding,
and a Pauli-frame update. The low-overhead cited layout deliberately mixes
6.6.6 and 4.8.8 regions, so its resource result is not a property of an
isolated 6.6.6 memory.

**Non-Clifford completion.** A prepared or distilled magic state, logical
Pauli measurement, and feed-forward supply the non-Clifford resource. The
fixed-block trapped-ion and multi-distance superconducting demonstrations
combine these resources with color-code Clifford operations; they do not
demonstrate a universal transversal gate set on one 2D patch. The
[operations ledger](pedagogy/transversal-clifford-and-operations.md) separates
the ideal code automorphisms from these protocol and hardware layers.

## Litmus questions

**Q1:** Why may the same face support define both an X check and a Z check?
**A:** Every face has even weight and distinct faces overlap on zero or two
vertices, so `H H^T=0` over `F_2`. The X/Z symplectic overlap is therefore
even for every pair.

**Q2:** Why does a red face not mean an X-type stabilizer? **A:** Red is one
of three geometric face colors and controls the colored-string dictionary.
That red support appears once as an X stabilizer and again as a Z stabilizer;
Pauli type is a separate label.

**Q3:** How do the formulas `n=(3d^2+1)/4` and `k=1` know about the boundary?
**A:** They count the retained vertices and independent clipped faces of this
specific modular triangular staircase. A different cut changes those counts
even if its bulk faces are also hexagons.

**Q4:** What does the left-boundary string prove about distance? **A:** Its
weight `d`, zero syndrome, and anticommutation with the conjugate string prove
an upper bound. Exact enumeration supplies the lower bound for `d=3,5`; the
distance-seven lower bound remains cited and claimed.

**Q5:** Why is a surface-code projection not already a color-code decoder?
**A:** One physical error contributes to several color-pair projections. The
projected matches are correlated and must be lifted to one correction whose
full color-code syndrome is correct, including the triangular boundaries.

**Q6:** Why does alternating S and `S-dagger` preserve an X face check?
**A:** Each four- or six-vertex face contains equal numbers from the two
bipartition classes. The local conjugation phases cancel and the result is
`X_f Z_f`, the product of two existing stabilizers on that face.

**Q7:** Do transversal H, S, and CNOT make the family universal? **A:** No.
They generate Clifford operations. A non-Clifford gate in the cited protocols
comes from a magic state, injection, distillation, switching, surgery, or
another resource outside the isolated constant-depth 2D stabilizer gate.

**Q8:** What exactly was demonstrated at distance three? **A:** The
seven-qubit patch is also the Steane block, so fixed-block experiments verify
encoded operations on the smallest family member. They do not by themselves
demonstrate increasing-distance suppression across the 6.6.6 family.

documents.title: Color boundaries, logical strings, and distance
documents.markdown:
# Color boundaries, logical strings, and distance

The shortest clean account keeps three labels distinct:

- **Pauli type** says whether an operator is X-like or Z-like.
- **String color** labels a sector of color-code excitations and deformations.
- **Boundary type** says which excitations may disappear at that edge.

A green face supports both X and Z checks. A green boundary is not therefore
an "X boundary." The anyon-condensation classification of
[Kesselring et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.00042) supplies the invariant
meaning: name a boundary by the excitation sectors it condenses, then use
color or Pauli words only after that dictionary is fixed.

## The declared logical pair

The constructor chooses every data qubit whose integer-grid column is zero.
For odd distance `d`, this left-side support `L` contains exactly `d` qubits.
Create two Pauli operators on the same binary support:

`X_L = product_(q in L) X_q`,

`Z_L = product_(q in L) Z_q`.

Every retained face meets the left side on zero or two vertices. Hence the
binary incidence vector `ell` satisfies `H ell^T=0`: `X_L` commutes with all
Z checks and `Z_L` commutes with all X checks. Their mutual symplectic
overlap is `|L| mod 2=d mod 2=1`, so they anticommute.

The patch has `k=1`. An anticommuting normalizer pair must therefore represent
its one logical qubit rather than a spare stabilizer pair. Multiplying either
operator by face stabilizers deforms the support without changing the
protected action. The colored-homology framework of
[Bombín and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0605094) explains
which deformations and endpoint condensations are topologically equivalent.

## Upper witness versus lower bound

The declared support proves

`d_code <= weight(X_L)=weight(Z_L)=d`.

It does not prove equality. Distance minimizes weight over every Pauli in the
normalizer but outside the stabilizer group. A different colored string, a
branched string-net, or a mixed representative could in principle be lighter.
The lower-bound step must exclude all of them.

The Atlas uses two evidence routes:

| instance | upper witness | lower-bound route | structured origin |
|---|---|---|---|
| `d3_triangle` | left side, weight 3 | exact CSS normalizer enumeration | verified |
| `d5_triangle` | left side, weight 5 | exact CSS normalizer enumeration | verified |
| `d7_triangle` | left side, weight 7 | triangular-family literature theorem | claimed, `chamberland2020triangular` |

For the first two instances, `qeclib.distance.exact_distance` enumerates the
CSS normalizer quotients and returns no lighter nontrivial logical. For the
thirty-seven-qubit instance, the constructor still recomputes the support,
zero syndrome, anticommutation, and weight seven. The missing machine-owned
fact is the exclusion of weights below seven. The card therefore routes the
family claim to `wanted:certified-lower-bounds` and does not relabel the cited
lower bound as verified.

## Why the smallest member is also Steane

At `d=3`, the three clipped faces have supports

`{0,1,2,3}`, `{1,2,4,5}`, and `{2,3,5,6}`.

Using them in both CSS sectors gives the seven-qubit self-dual Hamming/Steane
stabilizer code up to qubit and generator relabeling. This is an intersection
of descriptions: the Steane entry emphasizes a fixed algebraic block, while
this entry emphasizes the first patch in a growing local topological family.
It would be wrong to infer that every Steane-code protocol scales with this
geometry, or that evidence on one seven-qubit block demonstrates family
suppression.

## Boundary changes are code changes

On a closed color-code surface, global face relations alter stabilizer rank
and handles supply different logical classes. A triangular patch with Pauli
boundaries changes which sectors condense. Another finite staircase can keep
the honeycomb bulk but change the qubit formula or boundary check weights.
This is why the constructor rejects any boundary string other than
`three-color-triangle` instead of treating it as display metadata.

The practical test is algebraic: after changing a boundary, rebuild `H`,
recompute its rank and normalizer quotient, and re-establish the logical
representatives. Neither `6.6.6` nor a triangular outline is sufficient
evidence by itself.

documents.title: Decoding and syndrome-extraction boundaries
documents.markdown:
# Decoding and syndrome-extraction boundaries

For a CSS face matrix `H`, a Z-error support `e_Z` produces X-check syndrome
`s_X=H e_Z^T`; an X error produces the identical formula in the other sector
because `H_X=H_Z`. The symmetry of the static matrix does not make all
decoders or extraction circuits identical.

## The seven-qubit static syndrome table

For the distance-three patch, the three face rows are

`{0,1,2,3}`, `{1,2,4,5}`, and `{2,3,5,6}`.

A single Z error therefore produces:

| qubit | X-check syndrome `(f0 f1 f2)` |
|---:|---|
| 0 | `100` |
| 1 | `110` |
| 2 | `111` |
| 3 | `101` |
| 4 | `010` |
| 5 | `011` |
| 6 | `001` |

All seven nonzero three-bit syndromes occur once. This is the Hamming-code
view of the smallest patch. The same table diagnoses single X errors after
exchanging check sectors. For larger patches, bulk qubits touch three faces
while boundary qubits touch fewer; syndromes no longer form a single finite
lookup table that scales with `d`.

## Why color-code matching is not three independent matchings

A bulk error creates defects in three colored sectors at once. Treating each
sector as statistically independent throws away the fact that they share one
physical cause. The random-three-body Ising mapping of
[Katzgraber, Bombín, and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.4845)
keeps the joint constraint at the maximum-likelihood level, but a statistical
partition function is not automatically an efficient decoder implementation.

[Delfosse's projection decoder](https://arxiv.org/abs/1308.6207) maps
color-pair restrictions into surface-code problems. Matching those projected
defects is an intermediate step. The results must be lifted to one physical
color-code correction whose full syndrome is correct. On a triangular patch,
boundary connected components enter both projection and lifting; reusing a
closed-surface rule can create a correction with the wrong boundary class.

[Sahay and Brown](https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.11395) instead combine the three
boundary sectors in a matching graph embedded on a Möbius strip. The
nonorientable seam is bookkeeping for how a path changes color sector when it
crosses the folded boundary. It is not a claim that the physical qubits live
on a Möbius strip.

The idealized hexagonal-versus-square-octagonal comparison of
[Ohzeki](https://arxiv.org/abs/0903.2102) and the faulty-syndrome spacetime
gauge model of
[Andrist et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1005.0777) belong to different
statistical ensembles. Their estimates cannot be merged merely because both
papers use color-code language.

## Repeated extraction changes the data type

A static syndrome is one bit per face check. A repeated circuit produces a
time history of noisy outcomes. A detector is typically a parity between
outcomes whose ideal value should agree, possibly combined with flag or
ancilla information. One circuit fault may create several correlated
detectors and data errors.

Consequently a circuit-level decoder must retain:

1. the exact check-measurement schedule and boundary rounds;
2. data, ancilla, reset, gate, idle, and measurement fault locations;
3. how raw outcomes and flags become detectors;
4. correlations between detector events and final data observables;
5. the decoder graph or hypergraph and its weights;
6. the Pauli-frame convention; and
7. the declared logical failure event.

Flag circuits in
[Chamberland et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00355), superdense and
middle-out circuits in
[Gidney and Jones](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.08813), and detector-based
matching in
[Lee, Li, and Bartlett](https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.07482) therefore define
different inference problems even when their final stabilizer group is the
same.

## Threshold identity tuple

Before a threshold-like number can appear, record all of:

| field | required identity |
|---|---|
| family | tiling, finite boundary, and scaled instances |
| observable | fitted logical failure quantity and scaling variable |
| extraction | ideal syndrome, phenomenological rounds, or named circuit |
| noise | channel, locations, correlations, and probability normalization |
| decoder | algorithm, lifting/reconciliation, postprocessing, and version |
| source | figure/table/section and fit procedure |
| claim type | threshold, pseudo-threshold, one-point rate, bound, or hardware result |

The 2026-08-02 decoder sweep found several legitimate but incompatible
models. T102 introduces no threshold number because no single tuple belongs
to the bare check matrix. This is a positive epistemic decision: omitting a
number prevents a code-capacity transition, a faulty-syndrome result, and a
hardware scaling observation from being rendered as estimates of one
quantity.

documents.title: 6.6.6 color code — Level-2 map
documents.markdown:
# 6.6.6 color code — Level-2 map

The phrases "three-colored face code" and "transversal Clifford code" hide
several independent arguments. These pages separate constructor-owned
algebra from boundary, decoder, protocol, and hardware claims that remain
tied to literature.

1. [Face incidence, commutation, and parameter count](face-incidence-and-parameters.md):
   the modular triangular grid, clipped-face supports, exact `n` and face
   formulas, `H H^T=0`, independent rows, and `k=1`.
2. [Color boundaries, logical strings, and distance](boundaries-logicals-and-distance.md):
   the color/Pauli distinction, the declared boundary logical pair, why its
   weight is only an upper witness, and the exact-versus-claimed distance
   ledger.
3. [Decoding and syndrome-extraction boundaries](decoding-and-syndrome-extraction.md):
   the seven-qubit syndrome table, three-color correlations, projection and
   Möbius lifting, repeated detectors, and the threshold identity contract.
4. [Transversal Clifford gates and non-Clifford completion](transversal-clifford-and-operations.md):
   exact H, bipartite phase, and pairwise-CNOT Pauli maps; the 2D locality
   bound; and the additional resources consumed by surgery and magic states.
5. [Representations, variants, and realization ledger](representations-variants-and-realizations.md):
   colored homology, anyon condensation, folded surface codes, the
   three-body Ising model, tensor networks, neighboring tilings, and precise
   experimental claim boundaries.

## Reproduction contract

Run from the repository root:

```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
python atlas/color_666/pedagogy/reproduce.py
make verify-entry E=atlas/color_666
```

`reproduce.py` loads every shipped instance through the ordinary entry API
and independently rebuilds the integer-grid incidence data. It asserts site
and face formulas, support weights, three face colors, even pairwise
overlaps, GF(2) ranks, CSS equality and commutation, the boundary logical
pair, exact distances for `d=3,5`, the distance-seven upper witness, the
seven-qubit syndrome table, bipartite phase conjugation, pairwise-CNOT
symplectic action, scene/lattice correspondence, tour integrity, and T3
packet state. The ordinary entry verifier separately owns all structured
claims in `instances.yaml`.

The card omits `construction:` because the replay registry has no exact
adapter for "take this modular triangular vertex set, delete face centers,
clip six-neighbor supports, and preserve this row/qubit order." The
deterministic constructor plus the independent transcript verify the shipped
presentation without pretending a generic operation-tree replay exists. A
future canonical finite-patch equivalence path is routed to
`wanted:code-equivalence`.

The transcript verifies ideal logical action for this presentation, but it
does not promote the structured H, S, or CNOT operations from `claimed` to
`verified`. A shared gate referee must define equivalence up to stabilizers,
logical basis, phases, geometry permutations, and multi-block action; that
capability remains `wanted:transversal-gate-cert`.

## Provenance split

- **Recomputed facts:** all shipped site/face sets and orders; face weights
  and overlaps; incidence ranks; `n`, `k`, and CSS status; exact `d=3,5`;
  the distance-seven weight-seven logical witness; the seven-qubit static
  syndrome table; the H, bipartite-phase, and pairwise-CNOT Pauli maps for
  the declared logical basis; scene/lattice consistency; and tour structure.
- **Bounded facts:** none. No seeded search or statistical interval is
  introduced by this packet.
- **Claimed facts:** the distance-seven lower bound and family distance
  theorem; colored-homology and anyon-condensation interpretation; local-
  Clifford unfolding; decoder performance and circuit claims; logical
  surgery and magic-state protocols; and every hardware realization.
- **Routed gaps:** a general distance lower-bound certificate remains
  `wanted:certified-lower-bounds`; exact construction/equivalence replay
  remains `wanted:code-equivalence`; and generic logical-gate certification
  remains `wanted:transversal-gate-cert`. The broader `color_code_2d` entry is
  still a typed pending relation target.

No threshold number is promoted. Threshold-like results in the literature
differ by tiling, finite boundary, syndrome model, Pauli channel, circuit,
decoder, and fitted observable; the decoding page records the full identity
tuple required before any such number could enter the Atlas.

documents.title: Face incidence, commutation, and parameter count
documents.markdown:
# Face incidence, commutation, and parameter count

This page derives the exact finite object exported by `constructor.py`. It is
not a derivation for every lattice called a 6.6.6 color code.

## The integer-grid convention

Write the requested odd distance as `d=2t+1`, so the constructor bound is
`B=3t`. Start with

`T_B = {(r,c): 0<=c<=r<=B}`.

The point `(r,c)` is a face center when

`c mod 3 = 2-(r mod 3)`.

Every unmarked point is a data vertex. Face and qubit labels are both
row-major. Around a face center the ordered offsets are

`(-1,-1), (-1,0), (0,1), (1,1), (1,0), (0,-1)`.

All six neighbors survive in the bulk. At a side of `T_B`, exactly two are
clipped from a retained boundary face, giving a weight-four support. This
explains why the bulk name 6.6.6 coexists with four-body boundary checks.
The explicit triangular-family source is
[Chamberland et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1911.00355); the Atlas convention
then fixes the remaining ordering choices for replay.

## Count the face centers

Group rows by their residue modulo three.

| row | allowed face-center columns | count |
|---|---|---:|
| `r=3a` | `2,5,...,3a-1` | `a` |
| `r=3a+1` | `1,4,...,3a+1` | `a+1` |
| `r=3a+2` | `0,3,...,3a` | `a+1` |

The final row is `3t`. The `3a` rows run through `a=0,...,t`; the other two
classes run through `a=0,...,t-1`. Hence

`m = sum_(a=0)^t a + 2 sum_(a=0)^(t-1) (a+1)`

`  = 3t(t+1)/2 = 3(d^2-1)/8`.

The integer triangle contains

`|T_B|=(3t+1)(3t+2)/2`

points, so deleting the `m` face centers leaves

`n=|T_B|-m=3t^2+3t+1=(3d^2+1)/4`

data qubits.

| shipped `d` | `t` | faces `m` | data qubits `n` |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 1 | 3 | 7 |
| 5 | 2 | 9 | 19 |
| 7 | 3 | 18 | 37 |

The reproduction transcript obtains every entry in this table from the
constructor and checks the formulas independently.

## Why one incidence matrix commutes with itself

Let `H` be the `m × n` binary matrix with `H[f,q]=1` when qubit `q` lies on
face `f`. A CSS presentation with `H_X=H_Z=H` is valid exactly when
`H H^T=0` over `F_2`.

- A diagonal entry is the weight of one face modulo two. Every retained face
  has weight four or six, so it vanishes.
- Two distinct honeycomb faces are disjoint or share one complete edge. Their
  vertex supports therefore overlap on zero or two qubits, so every
  off-diagonal entry vanishes.

Thus the X check and Z check on the same face commute—their overlap is even—
and checks on different faces commute for the same parity reason. This is the
local algebra behind the self-dual CSS statement introduced by
[Bombín and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0605138).

## Why the face rows are independent

Suppose a nonempty set of face rows summed to zero. Choose an outermost face
in that set. Along the current exterior of the selected region, at least one
of its boundary vertices is incident to no other selected face. That qubit
would occur once in the sum, contradicting zero. Removing the outer layer
repeats the argument until no face remains. This boundary-peeling argument is
specific to the open triangle; a closed surface can instead have global face
relations.

The constructor enforces the same statement with `gf2.rank(H)=m` for every
built distance. Since X and Z generators occupy separate symplectic halves,
the full stabilizer rank is `2m`. Therefore

`k=n-2m=(3d^2+1)/4-2·3(d^2-1)/8=1`.

The three face colors do not appear in this rank subtraction. They organize
the topology of strings and boundaries; they do not contribute three
independent stabilizer copies or three logical qubits.

## What this calculation does and does not certify

It certifies the exact finite incidence presentation, commutation, and
logical dimension. It also gives bounded check weight: four at the boundary,
six in the bulk. It does not prove the family distance, the performance of a
decoder, a circuit threshold, or a logical gate under faults. Those require
the separate ledgers linked from the Level-2 map.

documents.markdown:
# Representations, variants, and realization ledger

Every row below describes the same code only within a stated domain. A useful
dictionary names both what it preserves and what it changes.

## Representation ladder

| picture | preserves | adds insight | must not be inferred |
|---|---|---|---|
| sparse CSS incidence | exact checks, ranks, logical quotient | machine-verifiable finite algebra | boundary physics not encoded by a matrix name alone |
| colored homology | stabilizer deformation classes and boundary endpoints | why three string colors describe one logical pair | a numerical decoder or circuit threshold |
| anyon condensation | excitation fusion and boundary absorption sectors | precise color/Pauli boundary and surgery language | that equally colored drawn edges are identical interfaces |
| folded surface codes | logical phase under local-Clifford equivalence | branching strings become attached surface strings | exact check/qubit order for this constructor |
| random three-body Ising | perfect-syndrome likelihood classes | three-way error correlations and phase transition | an efficient decoder or a circuit-level result |
| tensor network | local encoder tensors and operator pushing | how patches may be composed | inherited global parameters after contraction |

The homology source is
[Bombín and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0605094), the
unfolding dictionary is
[Kubica, Yoshida, and Pastawski](https://arxiv.org/abs/1503.02065), the
statistical model is
[Katzgraber, Bombín, and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/0902.4845),
the boundary classification is
[Kesselring et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2212.00042), and the tensor
construction is
[Farrelly, Tuckett, and Stace](https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.11996).

## Variant ledger

**6.6.6 versus 4.8.8.** Both realize the abstract two-dimensional color-code
order on trivalent, face-three-colorable cellulations. Their face weights,
vertex density, clipped boundaries, extraction circuits, and finite qubit
formulas differ. The comparative resource analysis of
[Bombín and Martín-Delgado](https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0703272) supports
the relation, not numerical transfer between entries. In particular, the
circuit study of
[Landahl, Anderson, and Rice](https://arxiv.org/abs/1108.5738) analyzes a
4.8.8 architecture; its numerical results are context, not 6.6.6 data.

**Triangular color boundary versus Pauli boundary.** The constructor fixes
one red, green, and blue side. A patch whose sides condense Pauli-labelled
sectors can have a similar outline and different logical/surgery behavior.
The boundary condition belongs in the formal identity.

**Seven-qubit Steane block.** The distance-three member is locally the same
stabilizer code up to row and qubit relabeling. Steane's algebraic
presentation and this family's growing geometry answer different questions;
fixed-block circuit evidence is not automatically scaling evidence.

**Hybrid lattice surgery.** Joining 6.6.6 and 4.8.8 regions deliberately
changes the local tiling to trade face weight against layout cost. The hybrid
device is neither an alias nor an isolated member of either uniform family.

**Tensor contraction.** Connecting encoder tensors removes or pairs legs and
creates a new global stabilizer code. Every resulting `n`, `k`, boundary, and
distance must be recomputed.

## Realization ledger

| platform evidence | established | did not establish |
|---|---|---|
| seven-qubit trapped-ion block | encoded operations on the smallest triangular color/Steane member | increasing-distance family suppression |
| trapped-ion fault-tolerant logical processor | Clifford primitives combined with magic-state preparation and injection | a universal transversal set on one 2D block |
| reconfigurable neutral-atom architecture | many small logical blocks and transversal inter-block operations | growth of one 6.6.6 memory patch |
| superconducting triangular processor | two finite sizes, repeated extraction, hardware-specific decoding, Clifford gates, injection, and logical teleportation | an extraction-independent threshold or asymptotic family constant |

The corresponding primary records are
[Nigg et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/1403.5426),
[Postler et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2111.12654),
[Bluvstein et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2312.03982), and
[Lacroix et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14256).

As of the 2026-08-02 realization sweep, no photonic 6.6.6 demonstration met
the Atlas distinction between a proposal and an executed logical code. The
same sweep found that only the superconducting record in this set directly
compared two color-code sizes; the earlier results remain important
fixed-block or multi-block evidence.

## The disciplined use of an equivalence

An equivalence is most useful when it tells the reader which computation to
move to another language. Unfolding motivates projected surface-code
decoding; anyon condensation organizes boundary joins; the Ising model
organizes likelihood correlations; tensor pushing organizes composition.
None authorizes copying a distance, threshold, or hardware number without
rebuilding the finite identity tuple. That restriction is the difference
between a representation dictionary and an accidental conflation of codes.

documents.title: Transversal Clifford gates and non-Clifford completion
documents.markdown:
# Transversal Clifford gates and non-Clifford completion

This page first derives ideal Pauli conjugation for the exact constructor
presentation. Fault-tolerant circuits, routing, repeated extraction, and
logical error rates are separate protocol layers.

## Hadamard from CSS self-duality

Physical H conjugates `X_q <-> Z_q` on every qubit. Since every face support
appears once in each CSS sector,

`H^(tensor n): X_f <-> Z_f`.

The stabilizer group is preserved exactly. The declared boundary operators
also swap, `X_L <-> Z_L`, so the logical action in this basis is H. The
transversal statement follows from `H_X=H_Z`; it does not require rotating
the triangular patch afterward.

## Phase from the vertex bipartition

Join consecutive vertices around each retained face. The resulting physical
vertex graph is bipartite. Under the constructor's row-major qubit order, the
two parts are precisely even labels `A` and odd labels `B`. Every weight-four
face contains two vertices from each part, and every weight-six face contains
three from each.

Apply

`U_S = product_(q in A) S_q · product_(q in B) S_q^dagger`.

Single-qubit conjugation gives

`S X S^dagger = i XZ`,

`S^dagger X S = -i XZ`,

while Z is fixed. If a face contains `a` vertices in each part, its X check
acquires phase `i^a(-i)^a=1` and a Z on every support qubit. Therefore

`U_S X_f U_S^dagger = X_f Z_f`,

`U_S Z_f U_S^dagger = Z_f`.

The left boundary alternates between the two parts and begins and ends in
`A`. It contains `(d+1)/2` A sites and `(d-1)/2` B sites. Its conjugation
phase is

`i^d (-1)^((d-1)/2)=i`,

so `X_L -> i X_L Z_L` and `Z_L -> Z_L`: logical S in the declared basis.
Swapping the physical S and `S-dagger` layers implements the inverse. The
reproduction transcript checks every face balance and logical phase for
`d=3,5,7` rather than inferring them from a diagram.

## Pairwise CNOT between aligned blocks

For a physical CNOT with control `c` and target `t`,

`X_c -> X_c X_t`, `Z_c -> Z_c`,

`X_t -> X_t`, `Z_t -> Z_c Z_t`.

Apply this pairwise to two copies with identical qubit order. A control X-face
check gains the corresponding target X-face check; a target Z-face check
gains the corresponding control Z-face check. Control Z and target X checks
stay in their original blocks. Thus the two-block stabilizer group is
preserved. Replacing a face support by the left-boundary support gives the
logical CNOT conjugation on `X_L` and `Z_L`.

"Transversal" here means one pairwise layer after corresponding qubits can
interact. A planar device may still need movement, routing, or a stacked
layout, and a fault-tolerant operation still needs syndrome extraction and
recovery around the layer.

## Why the native story stops at Clifford

H, S, and CNOT generate Clifford computation. They are valuable because the
physical action is unusually direct, but they are not universal.
The [Bravyi–König theorem](../../../foundations/bounds/bravyi-koenig.md)
places every bounded-spread constant-depth local logical gate in a 2D growing-
distance topological stabilizer family at the second level of the Clifford
hierarchy. T lies at the third level.

This is not a statement that all non-Clifford protocols are impossible. It
identifies what extra ingredient they must use:

- **Magic-state preparation or injection** supplies a non-stabilizer state,
  then consumes it through Clifford measurements and feed-forward.
- **Distillation** combines noisy resource states and postselection or error
  detection into a cleaner logical resource; the factory geometry and
  acceptance rule are part of the cost.
- **Code switching or gauge fixing** moves to a code with a complementary
  gate before returning; conversion faults and decoder side information are
  part of the operation.
- **Lattice surgery** measures joint logical Paulis through a temporary seam;
  repeated seam rounds and spacetime decoding supply fault tolerance.

The hybrid 6.6.6–4.8.8 surgery architecture of
[Thomsen et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.07806) and the color-code magic-
state factory of
[Lee et al.](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07707) retain these resource
boundaries. Their overhead is not another row in the static check matrix.
Flag-assisted preparation in
[Chamberland and Noh](https://arxiv.org/abs/2003.03049) likewise includes
redundant encoding, acceptance, and verification rather than turning a bare
transversal Clifford layer into a non-Clifford gate.

## Certification boundary

The executable transcript proves the ideal Pauli maps for the shipped basis.
The card still marks operations as `claimed` because the shared verifier does
not yet certify logical gates with phase, stabilizer equivalence, geometry,
multi-block alignment, and fault model all explicit. That general capability
is routed to `wanted:transversal-gate-cert`; local algebra evidence is not
silently promoted into gadget-level verification.
